decisions.rationale: id has distinct_count 9057 against dataset.row_count 9057 and null_rate 0.0, so it uniquely identifies every landed row; ident and iata_code show the same 9057 distinct count and remain available as alternate keys for a reviewer to measure against the warehouse.
dataset.duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across dataset.row_count 9057, so no exact duplicate rows exist in bronze and no dedupe step is proposed.

_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at and _airbyte_meta all carry is_airbyte_metadata true and describe the capture run (_airbyte_meta has distinct_count 1 with value '{}'), so all three are dropped from silver.

id landed as VARCHAR but all ten sample values ('10309', '1058', '111', ...) are integral digit strings with null_rate 0.0, so a strict INTEGER cast is proposed; any non-numeric value would fail the build rather than be silently coerced.
elevation_ft landed as DECIMAL(38,9) but every sample is integral (-1266.0 through -70.0) and min -1266.0 / max 14472.0 fit INTEGER, so the column is narrowed to whole feet.

latitude_deg (min -79.777778, max 82.517263) and longitude_deg (min -179.876999, max 179.9757) land as DECIMAL(38,9) but need at most three integer digits and six decimals, so they are narrowed to DECIMAL(9,6) and DECIMAL(10,6).

scheduled_service has distinct_count 2 with the complete distinct_values set 'no' and 'yes' and null_rate 0.0, so it is renamed to has_scheduled_service and cast to BOOLEAN with no third state to preserve.

local_code (null_rate 0.636635), keywords (null_rate 0.679585) and home_link (null_rate 0.749034) are more than half null but are retained as nullable text; no rows are dropped and no values are imputed.

icao_code (null_count 1237, null_rate 0.136579), gps_code (null_count 488, null_rate 0.053881), municipality (null_count 360, null_rate 0.039748) and wikipedia_link (null_count 1185, null_rate 0.130838) are partially populated, so they stay optional rather than failing the build.

purpose: silver_ourairports_airports is the cleaned airport reference table built from bronze.ourairports_airports (9057 rows): one row per airport identifier, with capture metadata removed, coordinates and elevation typed as numbers, and scheduled-service recorded as a boolean. It feeds geographic joins, airport lookups by ICAO/IATA/GPS code, and downstream gold aggregates by country, region and airport type.
usage: Join or look up on id (the declared grain, 9057 distinct values over 9057 rows); iata_code and ident are equally unique in this snapshot and can serve as secondary lookups. Filter on type (five values: heliport, large_airport, medium_airport, seaplane_base, small_airport) and has_scheduled_service to isolate commercially served airports. Consumers must handle NULLs deliberately in the code and link columns: icao_code, gps_code, local_code, home_link, wikipedia_link, keywords, municipality and elevation_ft are all partially populated, so inner joins on those columns will silently reduce row counts.
limitations: No deduplication is applied because duplicate_row_rate is 0.0; uniqueness of id is asserted from profile distinct counts only and must be measured against the warehouse before approval. elevation_ft is missing for 335 rows (3.7%) and is not imputed; local_code (63.7% null), keywords (68.0% null) and home_link (74.9% null) are sparsely populated and kept as-is. keywords remains unparsed free text of mixed shape rather than a normalized list, and the id cast from VARCHAR to INTEGER is strict: a non-numeric id outside the ten observed samples would fail the build. Link columns are not validated as reachable URLs.
